messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing (melting) point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water equilibrium:

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\;=\;\frac{T\,\Delta V}{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}
\]

with  

* \(T \approx 273\;{\rm K}\) (≈ 0 °C)  
* \(\Delta V \approx 1.6\times10^{-6}\;{\rm m^{3}\,mol^{-1}}\) (volume change from ice to liquid)  
* \(\Delta H_{\text{fus}} \approx 6.01\times10^{3}\;{\rm J\,mol^{-1}}\)

gives

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\;\approx\;7.3\times10^{-3}\;{\rm K\,bar^{-1}}
\quad\text{or}\quad
7.3\times10^{-8}\;{\rm K\,Pa^{-1}} .
\]

The pressure drop from 1 atm (101.3 kPa) to 10 kPa is \(-91.3\) kPa, so

\[
\Delta T \;\approx\; \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
          \;\approx\; 7.3\times10^{-8}\;{\rm K\,Pa^{-1}}\times(-9.13\times10^{4}\;{\rm Pa})
          \;\approx\;-0.66\;{\rm K}.
\]

Thus the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly

\[
\boxed{\;T_{\text{freeze}}\;\approx\;-0.7^{\circ}\text{C}\;}
\]

(≈ 272.3 K).

---

### Quick reference

| Pressure | Freezing point (°C) |
|----------|---------------------|
| 101.3 kPa (1 atm) | 0.0 |
| 10 kPa | –0.7 |
| 1 kPa | –1.4 |
| 0.6 kPa (triple point) | 0.0 |

> **Note:** The value is an approximation based on the linearized Clausius–Clapeyron equation. For highly accurate work, consult detailed phase‑diagram tables or perform a full thermodynamic calculation.
